correctness.rationale: Uniform-point rectangle covariogram gives exit-distance density (1+q-2qz) dz on z in [0,1], with moments T^p (p+2-pq)/((p+1)(p+2)) for all p>-1 and log moment log T-1-q/2 at p=0. Branch profiles Phi_(a,b,p) and Phi_(b,a,p) cover all unit directions and strict dominance Phi_(a,b)>Phi_(b,a) for q<1 reduces minimum to short-major profile, maximum to long-major. Log derivative has numerator t²[(p+2)q-(p+1)q²]-s² with positive denominator; the short-major profile has a unique strict interior min at q_min. For p<=2 the square endpoint comparison and a>b show global max only at ±long axis. For p>2 define w=1-pq/(p+2), B=w^(-2/p)-1, H=q²/B; its logarithmic elasticity E=qB'/B increases strictly from 1 to >2 by convexity of w^(-2/p), so H has one interior maximum and defines A_*. Comparing Phi(a,b,p)(q)/Phi(a,b,p)(0)=sqrt(1+q²/A²)w^(1/p) yields exact max regimes and six-way tie at equality; unique oblique maximum before transition is larger derivative root. SymPy exactly checked derivative and p=4 radical q_*, H(q_*) and numerical A_*=1.180800485353. Finite samples do not prove the all-parameter monotonicity; analytic convexity does.
